newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - France still mulls Thomson-CSF sale.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - France still mulls Thomson-CSF sale.

text.p: The French government is still studying the relative merits of a flotation or a private placement for privatising defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF, a government official said on Tuesday.

The official was responding to a report in the newspaper Les Echos that the Finance Ministry favoured a private auction with the highest price as the determining factor over other considerations such as industrial coherence.
"We are still studying the advantages and drawbacks of a flotation and a private placement," the official said. "No decision has yet been taken."
President Jacques Chirac launched a plan in February last year to restructure the defence industry around a few national champions, with a privatised Thomson group as its electronics giant.
Les Echos reported the auction would only be open to "qualified" bidders based on their ideas for the future of the company and a list of terms and conditions imposed by the government.
It said the government used the current Thomson-CSF share price to set a minimum price of 21 billion francs ($4 billion).
Thomson-CSF shares gained 1.95 percent to 172.50 francs on the stock market on the auction report.
An auction would rule out a public share offering, the solution favoured by Thomson's managers and French Industry Minister Franck Borotra, the paper said.
The government originally said last October it would sell Thomson-CSF parent Thomson SA to French conglomerate Lagardere for the symbolic sum of one franc.
Under the plan, Lagardere was to sell heavily-indebted Thomson unit Thomson Multimedia to Korean firm Daewoo Electronics.
France's independent Privatisation Commission objected to the latter aspect, forcing the government to suspend the sale and review its options.
An auction would also allow a fresh bid from engineering group Alcatel Alsthom, which was passed over in the first attempt to sell off the Thomson group. ($1=5.288 French Franc)
